thread:
mike: quick heads-up: saw a 12% p99 regression on qwen2.5 small-batch path after last kernel selector change.

saira: oh no. which selector commit? can you paste the perf job id?

mike: runner id `perf/run-2819` — baseline (old selector) p99=78ms, new selector p99=87ms on same hw. mean stable.

cheng: do we have batched vs streaming breakdown? could be batching heuristic picking larger groups and stalling on kv lookups.

mike: yeah, breakdown attached in logs below: `kernel_select: autokernel-v2`, `batch_policy: dynamic_250ms_or_16tok`, `kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.61`

perf-bot: summary for perf/run-2819 -> p50: 13ms (+1ms), p95: 44ms (+3ms), p99: 87ms (+12%).

eva: thanks. does this repro with forced kernel autoselect disabled (force kernel=best-static)?

mike: I ran that: force-static-kernel p99=79ms. suggestive of autokernel choosing a slower kernel path for some seq-lens.

cheng: any correlation with seq-length distribution? last change added a `head_kv_align` heuristic that groups by kv-head dim to pick optimized matmul kernels. might be picking a kernel that performs poorly on 2048 ctx.

saira: could also be tokenizer change — we saw more multi-ling tokens => longer effective seqs due to byte-level tokens.

mike: here's a small repro command I used:```bash
python tools/bench_infer.py --model qwen2.5 --seq-len 1024 --batch 4 --kernel-selector autokernel-v2 --policy dynamic_250ms_or_16tok
```

mike: profiler snippet (top ops):
```
matmul_kv_align_kernel  34%  (hot on heads with kv_dim%8!=0)
attention_softmax        18%
kv_read_lock             12%
copy_kv_to_device        10%
other                    26%
```

eva: that `matmul_kv_align_kernel` is the new special-case kernel we added when kv_dim != head_dim. If it's hitting due to head/kv mismatch, fallback should be the old generic matmul which was faster here.

cheng: agreed. PR #4012 added a heuristic that prefers aligned kernels to reduce scatter on kv offsets. but it assumed cache-hit patterns similar to llama. qwen has different kv stride, so alignment triggers more memcopy.

saira: can we add a quick AB test: revert the `prefer_aligned_kernels` flag for qwen variants and run the same perf job?

mike: I can run a canary with flag off for qwen2.5. scheduling now.

infra-bot: triggered perf/canary-1950004380 for qwen2.5 with prefer_aligned_kernels=false (nodes: g5.12xlarge).

perf-bot: canary result -> p99=80ms (down from 87ms), kv_cache_hit_rate unchanged. p95=45ms.

mike: looks like disabling the heuristic recovers most of the regression. I'll open a short-lived revert and add model-specific guard for qwen.

cheng: long-term we should enhance kernel selector to profile a tiny sample at init and pick kernel per-shard based on microbenchmarks. also adjust batching heuristic to avoid forcing larger batches when autokernel picks memcopy-heavy path.

saira: note: tokenizer edge-case too — we saw more CJK token run-length -> longer average prefix causing batch grouping to be skewed. recommend adding a tokenization-aware batch size cap for multi-ling workloads.

mike: agreed. action items:
- mike: open revert PR + model-guard for aligned-kernel (ETA 2h)
- cheng: prototype microbenchmark sampling in selector (ETA 2d)
- saira: add tokenization-aware cap to batch policy config and run synthetic CJK job (ETA EOD)
- eva: help validate on dedicated infra and confirm no regressions on other models (ETA tomorrow)

eva: add note to release doc: kernel-selector_v2 rollback for qwen until micro-sampling added.

mike: thanks. tagging @here in eng-runtime since this touches batching and kernel selection. :mag:

perf-bot: linked issue #4178 created -> "qwen2.5 perf regression: autokernel aligned-kernel selection causes p99 increase"

saira: feel free to ping me if you want help crafting the tokenization cap config.

mike: will do. closing thread once revert is merged.
